answer.rationale: p99 latency is 5x target during peak settlement traffic with a security patch that cannot be reverted. Rollback is ruled out. Circuit breaker would shed customer writes, violating the primary objective. Regional failover risks settlement consistency during peak. Routing read replicas doesn't address write-path latency. Headroom provisioning (memory_b3) successfully absorbed surge traffic without degradation before; adding capacity targets the root cause—insufficient write headroom during peak load with the new release's resource footprint. This preserves all writes, maintains the security patch, and has high precedent for success under similar load conditions.
